On Mon, Jul 16, 2028 at 06:31 Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Finnect alert. TL;DR: EU morning window, p99 ~2.1s on nightingale-v2; customer is impacted.

Quick SRE notes / analysis:
- Root pattern: heavy tail appears tied to longer context-length requests (avg seq len +45 tokens for impacted slice). The new attention kernel in v2 shows particular degradation on those sequences.
- Error rates are stable; mainly latency. No immediate OOMs or memory thrashing reported.
- Canary viability: we can route 10% of Finnect traffic to v1.9 within ~6 minutes; full rollback to 100% can be staged and completed in ~25–30 minutes.
- Risks: KV-cache incompatibility between v2 and v1.9 for streaming sessions — some sessions may lose cached context if switched mid-session. We can avoid this by applying the rollback at the routing layer (pin new sessions to v1.9) and letting existing sessions drain for 10–15 minutes.

Recommendation (recommended path):
1) Approve a time-limited SLA exception (customer-facing) for a 2-hour mitigation window to cover the rollback + validation period.
2) Initiate 10% canary to v1.9 now (ETA 6 minutes) — monitor p99 and tail latency.
3) If canary p99 drops to <=800ms within 10 minutes, expand to 100% over the next 20 minutes and close mitigation.
4) Post-mortem and model-onboarding review to follow.

I attach the rollback playbook with step checklist (rollback_playbook_v1.9.pdf).

— Hannah
SRE, Redwood Inference
